response:
It is completely understandable to feel torn in this situation. You care about your friend's well-being, but it is also valid to feel hesitant about lending more money when past loans haven't been repaid. While the final decision is yours, it can help to ask yourself if you are comfortable treating this money as a gift rather than a loan. If you cannot afford to lose that money, or if giving it will cause resentment and strain the friendship further, it might be best to gently decline. 

Setting financial boundaries is healthy and doesn't mean you don't care about your friend. If you choose not to lend the money, you can still offer support in other ways. You might help them look into local rental assistance programs, community action agencies, or food banks to help free up their cash for rent. Ultimately, protecting your own financial stability and peace of mind is important, and it is okay to say no.
